prose.title: The Champion Kept His Offense and Stood Still All Summer
prose.dek: Brian Cutting won the {{f.team.0004.hist_title_years}} title, kept every offensive starter from the title game, and spent just {{f.team.0004.faa_off_spend}} on offense at the Free Agent Auction. The preseason simulation ranks Pure Greatness {{f.team.0004.power_rank|ord}}, favorite in its division.

paragraphs: The champion's April roster looked like a champion's. Cutting carried {{f.team.0004.active_roster_opening}} active players, not yet enough for a full lineup, {{f.team.0004.cap_opening}} in salary, and {{f.team.0004.studs_opening}} top-twelve players: Drake Maye, a High-end QB1, Jahmyr Gibbs, an Elite RB1, Ashton Jeanty, and Justin Jefferson and Chris Olave at receiver. Zay Flowers, Davante Adams and Baker Mayfield were solid behind them. The one weak spot was tight end, where Dalton Schultz grades replacement-level.

Before the rookie draft Cutting made one trade. He gave Quentin Johnston's expiring rookie deal a one-year extension at {{f.team.0004.trade1_salary_out}} and sent him to The Long Haulers in May for a 2027 third. The trade bot was not grading deals yet; graded now as of that day, it comes out {{f.team.0004.trade1_grade}} for Cutting. The other three rookie deals that ran out, Darnell Washington, Quan Martin and Stetson Bennett, were let go. No cuts, and the Johnston extension was the only contract he signed in that stretch.

t.0004.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: In May Cutting tagged Myles Garrett at {{f.team.0004.contract_13198_salary}}. Justin Jefferson is in the last year of the back-loaded two-year deal he signed in 2025, the expensive year, and it runs out after this season.

Draft night was about next year. Cutting traded out of the second round three times, the trade bot grading them {{f.team.0004.trade2_grade}}, {{f.team.0004.trade3_grade}} and {{f.team.0004.trade4_grade}}, sending 2.06, 2.09, 2.12 and 4.12 away for 4.01 and three 2027 picks, a second and two thirds; 2.09 was his for thirteen minutes on the way to Gride. Add the third he got for Johnston and he goes into next spring with extra picks in both rounds. This year he made {{f.team.0004.rookie_picks_count}} picks from 4.01 down, Max Klare, Elijah Sarratt, Caleb Douglas, Cole Payton and Josiah Trotter, a class that will not touch this lineup. The only releases before the lock were Nic Scourton off the taxi squad and Zach Ertz, both at no cost.

t.0004.moves_s2.title: From the draft to the auction lock

paragraphs: Pure Greatness spent {{f.team.0004.faa_spend}} at the Free Agent Auction on {{f.team.0004.faa_lots_won}} players and did not buy a star. The most expensive was Aaron Rodgers at {{f.team.0004.faa_7836_price}}, who is on the bench. Mark Andrews cost {{f.team.0004.faa_13671_price}} to take over at tight end, James Conner and Chuba Hubbard {{f.team.0004.faa_13146_price}} each for running back depth, and Tyreek Hill, recovering from a torn ACL, {{f.team.0004.faa_12801_price}} as a flyer for later in the year.

Only the Andrews buy makes the lineup, and even he grades starter depth; the other nine offensive buys are bench depth, and the league table ranks the auction {{f.team.0004.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}} for how much it improved his offense. There was almost nothing to add to an offense whose only weak spot was tight end, and the Andrews buy did not fix it: he grades replacement-level, as Schultz did.

The contract work was light. {{f.team.0004.myac_faa}} auction buys got multi-year contracts, Andrews for {{f.team.0004.contract_13671_years}} years at {{f.team.0004.contract_13671_salary}} a year among them. He made no restructures and no waiver claims, and the four players released after the auction all went at no cost.

The lineup today has the same core as the April roster: {{f.team.0004.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Maye, Gibbs, Jeanty, Jefferson and Olave; running backs that rank {{f.team.0004.slot_rb_rank|ord}} in the league and receivers that rank {{f.team.0004.slot_wr_rank|ord}}; and {{f.team.0004.holes_today}} hole, still tight end, now Andrews instead of Schultz. Graded on MFL's projections, the defense is led by Andrew Mukuba, a High-end DB1, and Nik Bonitto, a Low-end DL1; Garrett, now a Ram, grades as a Low-end DL2 and was in his week one lineup. The kicker, Harrison Mevis, is a High-end PK1.

The injuries are mostly on the bench. Hill is out into October, so the forecast leaves him out of the first five weeks, and Conner is on injured reserve for four. The one starter with a designation is Christian Rozeboom, questionable with a foot.

t.0004.faa_value.title: What every owner's auction money bought

t.0004.moves_s3.title: From the auction to week one

captions.t.0004.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close; a buy that never makes the lineup adds nothing. What it bought grades each quarterback, back, receiver and tight end at his position: Elite is this year's separated top, which is one man at some positions and nobody at others, Very good the rest of the top twelve, Good the next twelve at quarterback, back and receiver (every team starts two, counting the superflex), Starter depth anyone else who starts somewhere in the league, and Bench depth the rest.

paragraphs: Cutting has been here from the start, {{f.team.0004.hist_first_season}}, {{f.team.0004.hist_seasons}} completed seasons. His one title is the most recent one, {{f.team.0004.hist_title_years}}, the same year he had the league's best all-play record, and it came three years after a runner-up finish in {{f.team.0004.hist_runner_up_years}}. Beyond the title: {{f.team.0004.hist_div_titles}} division titles, tied with Blake Bombers for the most in the league, {{f.team.0004.hist_playoffs}} playoff trips and a {{f.team.0004.hist_allplay_pct}} career all-play record.

The defending champion was the last team picked in the league's first Owner Divisional Draft, {{f.league.div_draft_pick_0004|ord}} overall, left on the board for HammerTime, whose owner had said in May that the last team left would be a strong one. Outlast PG Time holds the last two champions and The Long Haulers, and Eric Martel has called HammerTime against Pure Greatness a coin flip, then gave himself the edge. The simulation does not: Pure Greatness is {{f.team.0004.power_rank|ord}} in the league with a {{f.team.0004.sim_p_division}} chance at the division, against {{f.league.p_division_0005}} for HammerTime and {{f.league.p_division_0006}} for The Long Haulers, and {{f.team.0004.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds.

The division weeks are {{f.team.0004.div_weeks}}, with no byes in the first two. Week eight costs him Olave and Bosa, while HammerTime loses C.J. Stroud, David Montgomery, its kicker and a defensive back. Week eleven is his hardest, Maye, Adams and Mevis at once, though The Long Haulers lose four starters that week, A.J. Brown among them. Week fourteen, the last of the regular season, costs him only Mack Wilson and costs HammerTime Trey McBride and Javonte Williams. Across the five weeks he loses {{f.team.0004.div_week_own_byes}} starters to byes, HammerTime {{f.team.0004.div_week_byes_0005}} and The Long Haulers {{f.team.0004.div_week_byes_0006}}.

The next three years. 2027: Pure Greatness gets back to the final and loses it, and the tight end is still a hole lol. 2028: the division, and Maye is the best quarterback in the league. 2029: HammerTime takes the division back.

Week one is a division week, and it opened with {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done and {{f.team.0004.wk_points_final}} points in the bank for Pure Greatness. Maye threw three interceptions and still put up points.
